PullRequest.Title: agentHost: offer Computer Use on remote agent hosts
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Follow-up to #342312. Offer the Computer Use plugin to remote Copilot agent hosts as well as local hosts when `chat.agentHost.computerUse.enabled` is enabled. Previously, remote hosts ignored the setting and never registered the plugin.

- Sync the existing setting to remote hosts and remove the local-host-only registration gate.
- Clarify in settings and activation consent that Computer Use operates the machine running the agent host, not the client machine.
- Preserve the local-only macOS permission setup UI. Remote hosts use the plugin’s ordinary permission prompts.
- Keep the default off, explicit runtime opt-in, managed settings enforcement, per-application approvals, and Browser Use behavior unchanged.

## Validation

- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`: passed after installing missing dependencies with `pnpm install`.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `git diff --name-only -- '*.ts' | xargs pnpm run oxlint`: passed before committing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/agentHostConfigurationSync.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/computerUse.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotComputerUseActivationTool.test.ts --grep "Computer Use|ComputerUse|AgentHostConfigurationSync" --reporter dot`: passed, 47 tests.
- `./scripts/test.sh --isolate --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/agentHostConfigurationSync.test.ts --reporter dot`: passed, 24 tests.
- Pre-commit hygiene: passed.

## Manual testing still needed

Not yet validated end to end with a macOS client connected to a Windows devbox. This draft enables plugin registration; it does not provide a remote desktop session or bypass native desktop permissions.

1. Run matching builds containing this change on the client and Windows agent host.
2. Enable `chat.agentHost.computerUse.enabled`, reconnect/restart as needed, and start a remote Copilot session.
3. Wait for the plugin download, then run `/computer show` and `/computer on`.
4. Ask Computer Use to operate Calculator on the Windows host, approving any native prompts on that host.
5. Confirm the Mac desktop is not operated, and that disabling the setting removes the offered plugin after the client restarts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect/reconnect to a remote agent host and mirror Computer Use settings, including opt-in/opt-out changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing initialization sends the root-configuration patch without awaiting persistence. A setting change can request a runtime restart, but active turns and subagents finish first. Host-side configuration processing remains synchronous; disk persistence is queued off the immediate path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send RootConfigChanged over the existing agent-host protocol transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Connect/reconnect uses the same single combined patch as before, with one extra boolean for remote targets. A Computer Use setting change now contributes one patch per connected remote protocol client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Remote connect patches omitted Computer Use; changes to that setting did not themselves produce a remote patch. Local mirroring was already present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dispatch is not awaited by _forwardClientConfig. Host processing can request a deferred restart only when the effective startup configuration changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize existing root configuration and queue mkdir, temporary-file write, and atomic rename.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same write sequence per existing connect patch; one new sequence per forwarded remote Computer Use setting-change patch. No per-session file write is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Connect patches already persisted root configuration. A remote Computer Use setting change was not forwarded and therefore did not independently schedule this persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: JSON serialization happens while scheduling persistence, but asynchronous filesystem operations are queued and not awaited by action dispatch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of connected protocol clients/hosts and actual global-setting changes. Connect patches contain one additional boolean, not one operation per chat or setting. Existing root-config observers inspect registered sessions/chats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One combined configuration dispatch per client on connect; one patch for affected settings per change. Filesystem writes use the existing per-service promise chain. There is no new per-item dispatch loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration values come from the existing configuration model. Repeated equal values do not restart the runtime because CopilotAgentStartupConfig.equals rejects unchanged configurations. Workspace/folder/memory-only changes are not mirrored.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced registration scope through sync target filtering, protocol patch batching, host persistence, startup-config equality, and deferred restart ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host/session counts and storage latency are not measured. The added connect payload is constant-sized; additional standalone actions require actual global-setting changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Remote mirroring adds bounded work required by the feature, preserves batching, and does not turn connection synchronization into collection-sized boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start ordinary remote Copilot chats or list migratable chats with Computer Use enabled, on cold and warm plugin caches.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Shared runtime startup awaits one supported-platform sentinel probe alongside other startup assets. A missing plugin downloads in the background, so slow or failed downloads do not gate ordinary chats. Installation causes one shared-runtime restart at an idle point; if installation lands during startup, the start can repeat once before returning the client.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe the pinned plugin directory's .complete sentinel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One probe per supported enabled shared-runtime start; cold download resolution performs another probe. Calls are shared across chats through the shared client lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Remote shared-runtime startup skipped Computer Use resolution entirely; local enabled startup already used this exact path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial asynchronous probe is on startup's Promise.all path; archive download is not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET the pinned GitHub release ZIP and buffer/verify its SHA-256.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One download per cold enabled supported host installation, coalesced per agent. Zero on warm caches; failed attempts retry only when plugin resolution runs on a later runtime start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Remote hosts did not offer or download the plugin. Local enabled hosts already downloaded it in the background.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in the background. Does not block ordinary chat startup on network completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stage the ZIP, extract its platform subtree, write the sentinel, atomically publish the directory, and remove staging files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per successful cold installation, with file operations proportional to entries in the pinned archive. No extraction on warm starts and no external extraction process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This installation path existed for local enabled hosts but was unreachable from remote Computer Use registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background installation precedes plugin availability but not ordinary chats. The ZIP buffer and checksum work temporarily consume host memory/CPU.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the existing Copilot runtime and optionally stop/start it once to register a newly installed plugin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared runtime per ordinary host; a cold install can cause one extra start, not a restart per chat. A real setting transition can also request a restart, with reasons coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Remote hosts started the same runtime without the plugin and without an installation-triggered restart. The same bounded restart logic already served local enabled hosts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Normal startup is already required. An installation completed during startup can add one bounded restart to that startup; otherwise restart waits for all in-flight work to become idle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct enabled agent-host processes and the pinned platform/version archive, not the number of historical or active chats. Archive byte size and entry count control one installation's work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: _clientStarting coalesces shared-runtime starts. _computerUseDownload permits one in-flight installation per CopilotAgent; different hosts operate independently. Startup assets use Promise.all. ZIP extraction uses lazy entries and a throttler, not an unzip subprocess. Disable/disposal cancels the pending download.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persistent cache key is userDataPath/agent-host/computer-use-plugin/release.version/platform-arch with a .complete sentinel. Warm starts probe it and do not download or extract. Unsupported platforms return before filesystem/download work. Failed installs leave no complete sentinel; a later runtime start can retry, but every ordinary chat does not trigger a fresh start.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: production code and neighboring tests establish persistent cache reuse, one download per agent, background resolution, one-time startup retry, and restart deferral/cancellation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Pinned release sizes, download bandwidth, and restart duration were not measured. SDK-internal plugin loading is external to the inspected repository. Independent host count determines aggregate background downloads.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression. The remote feature deliberately enables one cached installation per host, preserves nonblocking downloads and coalescing, and introduces no per-chat installation or unbounded restart loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Launch a remote chat, show Computer Use activation consent, and enable the plugin after approval.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Non-ephemeral, non-scoped chat launch awaits the existing Computer Use tool-state check concurrently with other session preparations. Activation checks plugin state, waits for the user's answer, enables it, and confirms state before returning tools to the agent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: client.rpc.plugins.list to obtain runtime plugin state for activation-tool creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One list RPC per eligible chat launch while the setting is true; ephemeral and scoped-credential chats skip it. No per-plugin RPC fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Normally remote hosts never received the mirrored opt-in, so the existing setting check skipped this RPC. If a remote root config already explicitly enabled Computer Use, this unchanged RPC path could already run despite the previous registration gate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Included in concurrent session-preparation work before launch can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List plugins before activation, enable the single computer-use plugin after consent, and list again to confirm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Accepted activation uses two list RPCs plus one enable RPC. Concurrent attempts within one chat share the same sequence; declines do not invoke enable/postcheck.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Remote hosts did not register the built-in plugin, so successful activation was unavailable. The same bounded sequence already existed for local activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Activation completion awaits these ordered operations; waiting for explicit consent is intentional.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the existing chat-input request and receive the consent response through the agent-host protocol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One card per coalesced activation attempt. Changed descriptions add only a fixed-length explanatory suffix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same card transport and response mechanism existed locally; remote sessions could not activate an unregistered built-in. The text change does not add a new rendering or serialization loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User approval gates enabling the plugin, not unrelated chat initialization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Actual non-ephemeral chat launches and activation attempts; plugin-list payload scales with the runtime's installed plugin catalog. Historical chat restoration text processing does not itself invoke activation RPCs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Launch preparations use Promise.all. Activation has ordered precheck, user decision, enable, and postcheck; overlapping activation calls in the same chat share one promise and card. Distinct chats are independent and use the shared runtime.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Plugin state is read from the authoritative runtime, not a new shadow cache. _asking coalesces concurrent activation attempts within one chat. Decline is retained for that chat; subsequent calls may still check plugin state. No additional cache or retained catalog is introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in call counts, gating, launch reachability, and per-chat activation coalescing. Insufficient evidence of a new pathological SDK-internal cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime plugin-list implementation and latency are external; this repository establishes bounded RPC counts but does not establish an independently costly repeated catalog rebuild or remote client-host roundtrip per plugin.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added remote workflow reuses bounded state/activation RPCs required for consent, and the explanatory text does not independently increase expensive work or retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep native macOS permission setup local while remote Computer Use uses the plugin's ordinary prompts.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed guard prevents remote hosts from constructing CopilotComputerUsePermissionSetup. Local setup continues to be created only for enabled local macOS hosts; helper icon reading and setup dialogs remain in their existing setup lifecycle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the local macOS helper Info.plist and icon when the local permission setup requests them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing local setup reads only; zero such reads from remote setup after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous local-only registration gate also prevented remote setup creation. The new explicit local guard preserves that exclusion while enabling remote plugin registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the local permission-setup workflow owns these reads, not remote ordinary-chat startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one permission-setup owner per local enabled macOS agent, shared across chats. Remote hosts create zero such owners regardless of chat count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Singleton ownership per local agent. Remote hosts skip construction entirely; local setup behavior and cleanup are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: MutableDisposable retains the single local setup instance while enabled and clears it when disabled. No new remote icon/status cache or remote polling state is allocated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced explicit host/platform guard, singleton disposal ownership, setup callback, and client service's local-platform/status gating.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External plugin-native permission prompts were not inspected end to end. No repository evidence shows new client-side desktop probing, layout work, or retained setup resources.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression and no concrete old regression fix to record: the added guard preserves the prior local-only setup lifecycle rather than removing previously reachable expensive work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 10 changed files and every diff page against base 1cbf1bb378524fefc7e5c9a52a75cf67ba1d2509. Traced remote configuration transport/persistence, cold/warm plugin installation, shared-runtime startup/restarts, activation RPCs, and local permission-setup ownership. No high-confidence actionable performance regressions or concrete performance regression fixes found. Static review; external SDK/native-plugin internals and measured timings remain unverified.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
